title: Design a Distributed Lock Service (Chubby / Redlock)
subtitle: Leases, fencing tokens, Redis Redlock algorithm, and ZooKeeper ephemeral sequential nodes

stages.title: Stage 1 — Single Redis Key Lock (SETNX)
stages.bottleneck: If the lock holder process hangs or experiences a GC pause, the key expires, letting a 2nd process acquire the lock while Process 1 is still executing (Split-brain).

nodes.label:
Single Redis Node
(SET lock_key val NX EX 30)

stages.narrative: **Naive Single Redis Lock.** Acquires lock via `SET lock_key client_id NX EX 30`. If Redis master crashes before replicating to slave, lock is lost.

stages.title: Stage 2 — Fencing Tokens & Redlock Multi-Master Algorithm
stages.bottleneck: Process GC pauses still risk race conditions if backend storage does not enforce monotonically increasing fencing tokens.
stages.narrative:
**Redlock & Fencing Tokens.**
1. **Redlock Algorithm:** Client attempts lock on 3-5 independent Redis masters. Lock is granted if acquired on majority (`N/2 + 1`) nodes within lock timeout.
2. **Fencing Tokens:** Master returns a monotonically increasing integer (`fencing_token = 84`). Storage rejects writes with token ≤ 83.

stages.title: Stage 3 — ZooKeeper Consensus & Ephemeral Sequential Watchers
stages.bottleneck: High network traffic from polling locks.
stages.narrative: **ZooKeeper Ephemeral Sequential Nodes.** Clients create nodes under `/lock/lock-`. The client with the lowest sequence number holds the lock. Other clients set a Watcher on the node immediately preceding theirs, avoiding thundering herd polling.
